# Psalm 71 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 71:1 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** In-you YHWH I-have-taken-refuge; let-me not be-put-to-shame to-forever.
- **LOGOS:** In you, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame.
- **PNEUMA:** LORD, you are my shelter — don't ever let me be disgraced.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **EMET:** In-your-righteousness deliver-me and-rescue-me; incline your-ear to-me and-save-me.
- **LOGOS:** In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me; incline your ear to me and save me.
- **PNEUMA:** Because you always do right, come to my rescue. Listen to my cry and save me!

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **LOGOS:** Rescue me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless man.
- **PNEUMA:** My God, pull me free from the grip of those who are cruel and merciless.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 71:6 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Upon-you I-have-leaned from-birth; from-womb-of my-mother you-are my-severer; in-you my-praise continually.
- **LOGOS:** Upon you I have leaned from birth; you are he who took me from my mother's womb. My praise is continually of you.
- **PNEUMA:** I've depended on you from the day I was born — you brought me into this world. I will never stop praising you.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **LOGOS:** Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails.
- **PNEUMA:** Don't throw me aside when I'm old; don't abandon me when my strength gives out.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

- **EMET:** O-God do-not be-far from-me; my-God to-my-help hasten.
- **LOGOS:** O God, be not far from me; O my God, make haste to help me.
- **PNEUMA:** God, please don't stay far away! My God, hurry to help me!
